name: GP Alabama River Cellulose Mill - Perdue Hill AL

fieldNotes.truckGate: Single controlled access road off Highway 84 / Lena Landegger Hwy entering an isolated industrial mill; the long forest-buffered private road forms a controlled approach.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No Street View available (mill too remote, ZERO_RESULTS) - guard booth not directly confirmed; a 3,000-job pulp mill, one of the largest in North America, runs a staffed gatehouse by standard. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.scale: Pulp mills weigh inbound wood loads on truck scales; structures consistent with a scale/check area appear near the woodyard entrance. Inferred true; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Very large trailer drop yard NE of the process buildings - hundreds of semi-trailers in colorful rows confirmed at z20; clearly 50+.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Pulp/market-pulp mill ships baled pulp; dock banks present on the warehouse/baleline building but limited - 10-25 band, estimated ~18. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.railServed: Large rail yard with dozens of rail cars runs along the NE edge into the mill; rail is a primary mode for this cellulose mill.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: Mill is extremely isolated - surrounded by forest, no town nearby (Perdue Hill / Claiborne are small), cellular coverage likely weak. Medium confidence.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Large multi-building campus: pulp process buildings, woodyard, recovery, power, baleline/warehouse, plus extensive settling ponds and landfill.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long forest-buffered private access road provides ample queue depth before the gate.
fieldNotes.perimeter: Box covers the developed footprint - process buildings, woodyard, and trailer drop yard; excludes outlying landfill and pond areas to the S/SW.
